ci-bot: [PERF][pr#9876] microbench 'batch_affinity' crossed threshold: +27% (threshold 10%) — job perf/micro/batch_affinity

maria: saw this alert. assigning to perf-investigation. tagging runtime owners. :eyes:

alex: ugh. that's the PR that changed the batching heuristic (seqlen-prioritizer) right? merged yesterday into release/1.12.0

raj: yes, PR 9876 replaced the old affinity scorer with the new seqlen-weighted scorer. I ran a quick local microbench and reproduced the reg:
```
bench: batch_affinity
baseline: p50=1.40ms p95=3.20ms
current:  p50=1.78ms p95=4.10ms  (+27%)
config: --seq-prioritizer --batch-window=8 --kv-prefetch=true
```

lee: interestingly the KV hit rate dropped in the same run (kv_hitrate 0.84 -> 0.68). maybe the new ordering is evicting useful prefixes.

maria: can someone bisect to the exact commit? if it's the heuristic change we might need a targeted revert or a quick patch to preserve prefix locality. rollout for 1.12.0 is blocked until perf signoff.

raj: starting bisect now. plan: reproduce locally, then git bisect with microbench script and capture perf counters (SM occupancy, L2 miss ratio). will post findings.

perf-bot: bisect job queued: ci/perf-bisect/9876. output will be at ci.internal/redwood/perf/bisect/9876 (posting summary here when done)

alex: quick note — if this is kv-contention, there was also a quantization tweak earlier this week that changed buffer alignment. could be unrelated but worth checking.

raj: bisect hit commit a1b2c3d4 (the heuristic change). diff is small: reweights seqlen factor and flips the fallback kernel selection for >512 tokens. snippet: 
```
- weight = base + 0.6*seqlen_norm
+ weight = base + 1.2*seqlen_norm
 if (weight > 0.9) choose kernel="dense-autoselect" else kernel="streaming-quant"
```
This explains kernel switch for certain mixed-batch workloads which in turn disables aggressive KV prefetch in the dense path.

maria: thanks — that matches the drop in kv_hitrate. what's next? revert or hotfix?

raj: created PR 9889 to revert the kernel-select tweak and keep seqlen reweight behind an opt-in flag. running CI microbenches now.

ci-bot: PR 9889: perf microbench results: batch_affinity p50 back to 1.42ms (within noise). full perf job: OK.

maria: great. merging the revert and unblocking release canary, but we should follow up with a proper fix: ensure kernel selection doesn't change KV prefetch flags or port KV hints across paths. adding follow-up ticket.

lee: logging the action items: 1) short-term revert merged (9889). 2) add unit test that checks KV prefetch enabled for both kernels. 3) add microbench that simulates mixed seqlen batches with KV heavy traffic. 4) investigate quant alignment change as possible amplifier.

alex: nice work team. I'll coordinate canary run and confirm no regression in larger perf harness.

perf-bot: rollout-unblock request submitted for release/1.12.0 after revert; pending canary metrics.

maria: closing thread once canary green. thanks everyone. :rocket:
